turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Hello, am I speaking with Mrs. Khan from Chennai?

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Yes, this is she. Who is calling please?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: I am Anjali from the security desk at your bank. I am calling to confirm a transfer of twelve thousand rupees you made yesterday.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Oh, yes, I sent that to my grandson. Is there some problem with it?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: No, the transaction was successful, but we noticed a suspicious login attempt from another city shortly after.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: What? Oh my goodness, is my money safe?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yes, your funds are perfectly safe. I am just calling to remind you that the bank will never call you to ask for your OTP or PIN.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: I was worried for a moment. Do I need to give you some code to secure it?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Absolutely not, Mrs. Khan. Please never share any OTP, password, or Aadhaar details with anyone over the phone, even if they claim to be from the bank.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: I see. I have heard these things on the news, but it is good you told me.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: It is better to be cautious these days. Just keep your details private and you will be fine.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Thank you for the warning, Anjali. I will remember this.
